title: Recycling Hub — UI/UX re-audit
environment: Local production frontend at 127.0.0.1:3101; isolated .next-ui-validation output; synthetic authenticated role and API fixtures. Public page rendering uses local application code. No live business API writes, account changes or implementation changes.
method: Desktop 1440×1000 and mobile 390×844 browser inspection, keyboard interactions, controlled API failures, source review, and 69 passing existing mocked UI regression tests. Source-only findings are labelled individually. This is a usability/accessibility review, not a WCAG certification, user study or backend permission/security audit.

issues.title: Failed delivery queue becomes a real zero
issues.problem: With the delivered-orders API returning 503, “Awaiting close” displays 0. The preview section disappears because deliveries.length is zero and loading has ended.
issues.impact: The receiving officer can conclude there is no work even though the system cannot establish the queue size.
issues.recommendation: Pass the queue error into the metric card, show “Unavailable” and Retry, and keep the queue error visible independently of its item count. Preserve the last successful count only when clearly marked stale.
issues.acceptance: A failed first load never displays a successful zero; retry recovers both count and preview.

issues.title: Dashboard aggregates can load forever after failure
issues.page: Receiving overview; admin, staff and super-admin aggregate hooks
issues.status: Browser verified for receiving; source verified elsewhere
issues.problem: Receiving “Closed this month” remains a skeleton after the aggregate request fails. Admin and super-admin aggregate hooks also swallow failures with .catch(() => {}).
issues.impact: Users cannot distinguish a slow request from a failed service and cannot recover the affected cards.
issues.recommendation: Give aggregate hooks explicit loading/error/refetch state; wire every KPI and status chart to the shared error-and-retry presentation already used in accounting.
issues.acceptance: A settled failed aggregate displays an error rather than a skeleton; retry affects all dependent cards.

issues.title: Mobile request actions open outside the viewport
issues.problem: At 390px, the 208px menu starts at approximately −80px. Edit, Create order and Cancel request labels are cut off. The menu aligns its right edge to a left-aligned trigger without clamping to the viewport.
issues.impact: Important request actions become hard to identify and operate on a phone.
issues.recommendation: Clamp the menu to a 12–16px viewport gutter, flip horizontal alignment near the left edge and limit height when space is short. Preserve desktop styling and the portal that prevents table clipping.
issues.acceptance: All menu items remain fully visible at 320, 390 and 768px, including after scrolling.

issues.title: Menu semantics promise keyboard behavior that is missing
issues.problem: Opening Actions with Enter and pressing ArrowDown leaves focus on the trigger. The panel declares role="menu" and items declare role="menuitem", but there is no arrow-key navigation or initial item focus.
issues.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users encounter an unfamiliar, inefficient control.
issues.recommendation: Implement initial focus, ArrowUp/Down, Home/End and Escape focus restoration; alternatively use a disclosure of ordinary buttons with matching semantics. Avoid mixing the two patterns.
issues.acceptance: Keyboard users can enter, traverse, activate and dismiss the menu; closing consistently restores trigger focus.

issues.title: Account status control ignores the visible permission gate
issues.page: Admin → Users → another administrator’s Active badge
issues.status: Browser affordance + source verified; mutation not submitted
issues.problem: The other administrator row correctly hides Edit/Delete, yet its Active badge remains an enabled button. That button is outside canManageUser and calls the update handler.
issues.impact: The interface invites an action that its own row-level permission model says the actor cannot perform. Users get a preventable server rejection.
issues.recommendation: Apply the same capability check to status changes. Render a noninteractive badge for protected accounts and explain the restriction in the detail view. Continue enforcing authorization on the server.
issues.acceptance: An admin cannot initiate a status change for a protected administrator; allowed rows retain accessible controls.

issues.title: Draft edits disappear on back navigation
issues.page: Profile edit: /profile/edit; other long forms require follow-up
issues.problem: After changing Full name, selecting Back to profile navigates away without a warning or draft preservation. The browser interaction confirmed no dialog.
issues.impact: Users lose entered information when they navigate away accidentally. The risk increases on long forms and mobile.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a shared dirty-form guard for in-app navigation and refresh/close, with Stay/Discard actions. Consider restoring local drafts for the multi-step request form.
issues.acceptance: A modified profile prompts before discarding; unchanged forms navigate immediately; saving clears dirty state.

issues.title: Material lookup has no recoverable error state
issues.page: New request / edit / order material category picker
issues.status: Source verified; outage interaction not browser-tested
issues.problem: usePickupCategories has then/finally but no catch, error or retry. Rejection ends loading and leaves an empty category list; its returned contract cannot explain failure.
issues.impact: Staff can mistake a service outage for missing material configuration and be unable to complete an order.
issues.recommendation: Return loading/error/refetch from the hook; show a local error with Retry beside the picker. Distinguish “No active materials” from “Could not load materials.” Preserve draft orders while retrying.
issues.acceptance: Empty successful results and failed requests render different states, and retry preserves entered quantities and photos.

issues.title: Photo pickers lack visible keyboard focus and linked guidance
issues.status: Source verified; profile upload affordance visually inspected
issues.problem: The focusable file input is sr-only and separate from its visible label. No focus-within treatment marks the visible upload control, and the pickup photo error/helper text is not associated with the input.
issues.impact: Keyboard focus can appear to disappear at uploads; screen-reader users may not receive the photo requirement or its error in context.
issues.recommendation: Use a shared file-input component with visible focus on its label, an explicit accessible name, aria-describedby for requirements/errors and aria-invalid on failure. Preserve native file-picker behavior.
issues.acceptance: Tab focus is visibly apparent; the input announces its label, allowed formats, count requirement and validation error.

issues.title: Image upload requirements are not explained before selection
issues.status: Source verified; no real upload attempted
issues.problem: The controls accept image/* but do not state a size limit or enumerate supported formats. The shared storage hook sends metadata to presigned upload without a local file-size check.
issues.impact: Users discover avoidable failures only after selecting or transferring a large or unsupported image.
issues.recommendation: Display the backend-supported types and size cap beside the picker; validate against that same contract before uploading. Show thumbnail/filename, pending state and a clear retry path. Do not invent different limits in each uploader.
issues.evidence: Concrete example: “Upload photo” / “Add photo” with no size guidance
issues.acceptance: An oversized or unsupported file produces an immediate, understandable error before a storage transfer starts.

issues.title: Receiving quantity omits its measurement unit
issues.problem: An item with collected_quantity 2.50 and quantity_unit kg displays “Laptop — 2.50”. Only a summary and one quantity are shown, including for multi-item orders.
issues.impact: The officer cannot reliably tell kilograms from units or verify each material line.
issues.recommendation: Render each item as category + received quantity + unit, using the shared quantity formatter. Where delivered totals are used, make the total’s unit explicit and avoid combining incompatible units.
issues.acceptance: Mixed kg/unit fixtures show each item’s value and unit unambiguously on desktop and mobile.

issues.title: Verification action lacks an inspection step
issues.status: Browser affordance + source verified; close not submitted in this audit
issues.problem: The queue offers a direct close icon but no request-detail link or evidence-review panel. It shows customer, summary, store and status, without a way to inspect delivery proof or all material lines on this page.
issues.impact: An officer is asked to certify receipt with limited context; mistakes may only be discovered after closure. The precise evidence needed still needs operations input.
issues.recommendation: Add a receiving-specific read-only review panel showing order code, materials/units, drop-off time, driver and available proof. End with a clearly labelled Verify and close action. Confirm the required evidence with receiving staff before designing mandatory fields.
issues.acceptance: An officer can inspect available delivery evidence and the exact order before closing; incomplete evidence has an explicit policy.

issues.title: Repeated receiving buttons are not uniquely named
issues.page: Receiving queue for one customer with multiple orders
issues.problem: Both C1000 and C1001 have the accessible name “Verify and close delivery from Test Customer”. The visual action is only a double-check icon.
issues.impact: Screen-reader users cannot distinguish the two actions by name, and new users must infer what the icon means.
issues.recommendation: Include the order code in the accessible name and tooltip; consider a compact visible “Verify” label on cards. Keep the existing 44px target and pending-submission protection.
issues.acceptance: Each action is uniquely identifiable by order code and customer in the accessibility tree.

issues.title: BM selection still produces mixed-language screens
issues.page: Users, Vehicles, Categories, Profile, sidebar and pagination nouns
issues.problem: BM navigation surrounds English headings, filters and form sections. Examples include “Vehicles”, “PEOPLE”, “Edit profile” and “Memaparkan … users”.
issues.impact: Users must switch language mentally within one task; the language selector promises more consistency than these modules deliver.
issues.recommendation: Finish translations by complete workflow, including navigation, headings, helper text, error copy, status labels and plural nouns. Preserve customer names, addresses and notes. Add a locale completeness check for static interface keys.
issues.acceptance: A BM task can be completed through list, detail, form, errors and success feedback without unexplained English UI copy.

issues.title: Generic translation notice consumes mobile form space
issues.page: BM pickup request creation and other portal pages
issues.problem: The same broad English-availability banner appears even on the extensively translated pickup form. On the 390×844 first screen, banner/back link/header/stepper/footer leave only a narrow slice of the first field visible.
issues.impact: The actual task starts far below the top; repetitive chrome increases scrolling and weakens confidence in translation readiness.
issues.recommendation: Track language availability by module and show a concise contextual notice only where needed. Tighten the mobile form header/stepper while preserving required-field guidance and sticky actions. Check focused fields above both sticky bars.
issues.acceptance: The first required field and its label are comfortably visible on a standard phone without losing context or accessible warnings.

issues.title: Optional-note disclosure has untranslated and duplicated labels
issues.problem: The collapsed row hardcodes “(optional)” and repeats the note label when expanded. The control uses a switch to show/hide an input rather than change an underlying preference.
issues.impact: BM users see English fragments; the expanded field is visually repetitive, and the switch’s purpose can be mistaken for a stored setting.
issues.recommendation: Use a translated “Add note (optional)” disclosure button with aria-expanded/aria-controls, a single field label and retained draft text when collapsed.
issues.acceptance: The disclosure is translated, clearly expands content, and hiding it never silently erases a note.

issues.title: List context is lost on refresh or returning from detail
issues.page: Pickup request, user and category lists
issues.status: Source verified; refresh/back interaction not separately exercised
issues.problem: Search, page and filters are kept in component state. Pickup requests persist only the active tab from the URL. Most list context cannot be bookmarked or reconstructed after remount.
issues.impact: Users doing repeated review work may have to re-enter a search and locate their previous page.
issues.recommendation: Put meaningful search/filter/page state in query parameters; initialize from them and reset page only when criteria change. Restore scroll position when returning from detail.
issues.evidence: Concrete example: filtered request list → detail → remounted list
issues.acceptance: A copied URL restores search, filters and page; back navigation returns to the same working context.

issues.title: Vehicle lookup requires paging through the fleet
issues.problem: The vehicle list has pagination but no search, status or assignment filters. The component notes that the server currently lacks these query options.
issues.impact: Finding a plate or an unassigned vehicle becomes slow as fleet size grows.
issues.recommendation: Add server-backed plate/driver search and active/assigned filters, following existing list patterns. Reset to page one when criteria change and give a clear filtered empty state.
issues.acceptance: A plate can be found across the whole fleet rather than just the current page; filter state survives detail navigation.

issues.title: Error state still claims a zero-result list
issues.page: Categories; source pattern also in Users and Vehicles tables
issues.status: Browser verified for categories; source verified for others
issues.problem: A failed category request shows a red error and Retry above “0 categories” and “Page 1 of 1”. The footer is rendered independently of error.
issues.impact: Users receive contradictory information: the system both failed to load and appears to confirm an empty dataset.
issues.recommendation: Hide result totals and pagination on an initial failure. If retaining successful previous data, label it stale and avoid presenting it as fresh. Apply one shared list-state contract.
issues.acceptance: Failed initial requests show no successful result count; empty successful responses still show an accurate empty state.

issues.title: Category parent can disappear when it is off-page
issues.status: Browser with synthetic off-page parent + source verified
issues.problem: Parent names are resolved only from categories on the loaded page. A valid parent ID absent from that page renders the same dash as “no parent”.
issues.impact: Staff can misunderstand the hierarchy and make unnecessary corrective edits.
issues.recommendation: Return parent id/name together from the API, or maintain a complete parent lookup independent of page/search. Distinguish absent parent from unresolved metadata.
issues.acceptance: A child’s parent name remains correct across page changes and filtered lists.

issues.title: Tabs do not expose selected state or panel relationships
issues.page: Shared Tabs: requests, request detail, users, notifications
issues.problem: The shared control uses ordinary buttons and a decorative active underline, without tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, aria-selected or arrow-key behavior.
issues.impact: Assistive technology cannot identify the selected tab or connect it to the changing content.
issues.recommendation: Implement an accessible tabs primitive with selected state, linked panel IDs and keyboard navigation. Use navigation links instead where a control represents a page rather than a local panel.
issues.acceptance: Selected tab and corresponding panel are announced; keyboard activation and focus follow one consistent pattern.

issues.title: Requested time is hidden behind a date-only display
issues.problem: The fixture requests 23 Nov 2026 at 02:00 UTC. The detail view shows only “23 November 2026”; the time exists in the time element’s title but is not visible in the main value.
issues.impact: Staff can overlook the customer’s preferred time, especially on touch devices where hover titles are unavailable.
issues.recommendation: Show date plus local time and a clear Malaysia-time label where this value influences scheduling. Distinguish customer preference from driver-confirmed time.
issues.acceptance: A requested timestamp visibly shows the intended date/time; null values remain explicit; driver confirmation is labelled separately.

issues.title: Shared validation mixes browser bubbles with form errors
issues.page: New pickup request → Continue with empty fields
issues.problem: An empty Continue produces a page alert plus a native validity bubble. ValidatedForm validates during submit capture before the step hook, calls reportValidity and highlights one control at a time. The mobile screenshot places feedback near sticky action/navigation areas.
issues.impact: Feedback location and behavior vary between generic controls and step-specific validation; users may need repeated attempts to discover all missing fields.
issues.recommendation: Use the external validation mode for the stepped form, with one error map, inline messages and a linked summary for the current step. Scroll the focused control above sticky elements. Preserve current blur validation and input values.
issues.acceptance: One submission exposes all current-step errors consistently; focus lands on a visible invalid field without competing native bubbles.

issues.title: Responsive table behavior depends on English headings
issues.status: Source verified; translated receiving card illustrates presentation difference
issues.problem: The action-row heuristic recognizes only an empty header or /^actions$/i. “Tindakan” and singular “Action” become ordinary labelled cells unless a caller sets data-card-role explicitly.
issues.impact: Equivalent tables diverge in mobile layout and touch-target treatment as localization changes, creating fragile reuse.
issues.recommendation: Define column/card roles explicitly in table metadata or props. Generate both desktop headings and mobile labels from that schema rather than parsing rendered text. Preserve the successful card layout.
issues.acceptance: Translated and English variants produce identical semantic card roles and action placement without string matching.

issues.title: Permission restrictions lack a user-facing explanation
issues.problem: A protected administrator row shows only View, while a staff row shows View/Edit/Delete. There is no explanation of why management actions are absent.
issues.impact: Users can interpret the difference as missing functionality or a loading problem.
issues.recommendation: On the read-only detail view, add a concise capability message such as “Only a super administrator can edit this account.” Avoid disabled controls without an explanation; centralize the capability rule.
issues.acceptance: Read-only users understand who can perform the restricted action and how to obtain help.
